title: Where to? (Wohin? Ins Büro!)
summary: Two questions, two cases: Wo? takes the dative (im Büro), Wohin? the accusative (ins Büro). The old chunks ins Kino and in die Stadt, explained at last. Going places at work and after work.
goals: Tell Wo? (where) from Wohin? (where to) with in, an and auf
Say where you're going with the accusative: ins Büro, in die Kantine, in den Keller
Understand the chunks ins Kino, in die Stadt and ins Museum
Use the short forms ins and ans

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A2, chapter 10: How do you live? (Der Umzug): two-case prepositions

sections.title: Wo? or Wohin?
sections.text:
Unit 6 answered **Wo?** (where) with the dative: [[Ich bin im Büro.]] Now **Wohin?** (where to). After [[in]], [[an]] and [[auf]], going **to** a place takes the **accusative**:
- [[Wo bist du?]] - [[Im Büro.]] (dative: [[im]] = [[in dem]])
- [[Wohin gehst du?]] - [[Ins Büro.]] (accusative: [[ins]] = [[in das]])

You've used this since Unit 3 as a fixed phrase: [[Wollen wir ins Kino gehen?]] [[ins Kino]] is [[in das Kino]] in the accusative, because you go **to** the cinema. The same goes for [[in die Stadt]] and Unit 9's [[ins Museum]]. They aren't chunks any more: they follow this rule.

sections.title: The question decides, not the verb
sections.text:
Ask: does it happen **in** a place (Wo?), or does someone or something go **to** a new place (Wohin?)?
- [[Ich laufe im Park.]] = I'm running in the park. I stay inside it: Wo?
- [[Ich laufe in den Park.]] = I'm running into the park. I go there: Wohin?
- [[Ich arbeite im Büro.]] but [[Ich gehe ins Büro.]]

Two things stay as you know them:
- [[zu]] and [[nach]] always take the dative, also for Wohin? (Unit 6): [[zum Arzt]], [[nach Hause]].
- [[ankommen]] answers Wo?, because you're already there when you arrive: [[Ich komme um neun im Büro an.]]

Russian does the same with в, на, под and за: где? в офисе, на столе, под столом; куда? в офис, на стол, под стол. After these words, куда? = [[Wohin?]] = accusative. Like [[zu]], Russian к takes the dative: к врачу = [[zum Arzt]]. German does it with all nine words of this unit (lessons 2 and 3 bring the rest), while Russian над, перед and между never switch.

sections.title: Going places at work
sections.text:
- [[Ich gehe in die Kantine.]] ([[die Kantine]] = canteen) - [[Ich esse in der Kantine.]]
- [[Ich gehe kurz in den Keller.]] ([[der Keller]] = basement, cellar) - [[Das Papier ist im Keller.]]
- [[Ich gehe in den zweiten Stock.]] Like [[im zweiten Stock]] (Unit 6), the ordinal ends in -en after [[den]].
- [[Ich gehe kurz auf die Toilette.]]
- [[Im Mai fahren wir auf die Messe.]] ([[die Messe]] = trade fair; Munich has several big ones) - [[Ich war drei Tage auf der Messe.]]
- [[Mein Auto ist kaputt. Ich bringe es in die Werkstatt.]] ([[die Werkstatt]] = garage for repairs, workshop) - at home it stands [[in der Garage]] ([[die Garage]]).

sections.title: After work and at the weekend
sections.text:
- [[ins Theater]], [[ins Rathaus]] (town hall), [[ins Kaufhaus]] (department store), [[ins Einkaufszentrum]] (shopping centre), [[ins Fitnessstudio]] (gym)
- [[in die Bibliothek]] (library), [[in die Disco]] (club), [[in eine Ausstellung]] ([[die Ausstellung]] = exhibition)
- [[in den Zoo]], [[in den Wald]] (forest), [[in den Kindergarten]] (nursery school): [[Ich bringe die Kinder in den Kindergarten.]]
- with [[an]]: [[an den See]], [[ans Meer]]; with [[auf]]: [[auf den Markt]], [[auf eine Party]]
- a trip: [[ins Ausland]], [[in die Berge]], and countries with an article: [[in die Schweiz]], [[in die Türkei]]. Countries without one take [[nach]]: [[nach Österreich]].
- and at night: [[Ich gehe ins Bett.]] - [[Ich liege im Bett.]]

[[in der Nähe]] (nearby) is Wo?: [[Gibt es hier in der Nähe eine Bibliothek?]]

sections.title: Short forms
sections.text: [[ins]] = [[in das]] and [[ans]] = [[an das]], like [[im]] and [[am]] in the dative. In speech you'll also hear [[aufs]] = [[auf das]]. Feminine and plural never shorten: [[in die Stadt]], [[in die Berge]].

sections.title: Wo ... hin?
sections.text: In speech, [[wohin]] often splits in two: [[Wo gehst du hin?]] = [[Wohin gehst du?]] It starts with [[wo]], but it asks **where to**, so the answer takes the accusative: [[In die Kantine.]] Listen for the [[hin]] at the end.

items.de: Wohin gehst du? - In die Kantine.
items.en: Where are you going? - To the canteen.

items.de: Wo ist Eva? - Sie ist in der Kantine.
items.en: Where's Eva? - She's in the canteen.

items.de: Am Wochenende fahren wir an den See.
items.en: At the weekend we're going to the lake.

items.de: Ich bringe die Kinder um acht in den Kindergarten.
items.en: I take the children to nursery school at eight.

items.de: Wir gehen heute Abend ins Theater.
items.en: We're going to the theatre tonight.

items.de: Ich war gestern in der Bibliothek.
items.en: I was at the library yesterday.

items.de: Wo gehst du hin? - Ins Fitnessstudio.
items.en: Where are you off to? - To the gym.

items.de: Ich komme um neun im Büro an.
items.en: I get to the office at nine.
Where are you? - In the office.

items.de: Ich gehe kurz in den Keller.
items.en: I'm just popping down to the basement.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I'm going to the canteen now.
items.explanation: Wohin? + accusative: die Kantine stays die. For Wo? it would be the dative: in der Kantine.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap with one word (a short form): We're going to the theatre tonight.
items.explanation: das Theater, and you go there (Wohin?): in das Theater = ins Theater.

items.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Ich arbeite heute in das Büro.
items.explanation: You work in the office: that happens in a place, so Wo? + dative: im Büro. ins Büro is for going there: Ich gehe ins Büro.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: At the weekend we're going to the forest.
items.text: Am Wochenende gehen wir in ___ Wald.
items.explanation: der Wald, and you go there (Wohin?): accusative, in den Wald. Wo? would be im Wald.

items.audio: Ich bin heute nicht im Büro. Ich bin auf der Messe.
items.question: Where is the person today?
items.explanation: Ich bin auf der Messe = I'm at the trade fair. Wo? + dative: auf der Messe. Going there would be auf die Messe.
